newsitem.title: CHINA: China sees lower inflation in 1997, stable rates.
newsitem.headline: China sees lower inflation in 1997, stable rates.

text.p: China's retail price inflation is expected to fall below five percent in 1997 and interest rates would remain stable, Qiu Xiaohua, chief economist of the State Statistical Bureau said on Friday.
"We can be fairly certain that inflation will at least be around five percent," Qiu said. "Although based on current circumstances, an inflation rate of three to four percent is possible."
China's benchmark retail price inflation rate was a year-on-year 2.6 percent in the first quarter, while first quarter consumer price inflation was 5.2 percent.
Consumer price inflation in March alone stood at 4 percent, while retail price inflation was 1.7 percent in March.
Beijing has set a target of 6.0 percent inflation in 1997 after the rate was 6.1 percent in 1996, down from 14.8 percent the year before.
Qiu said he did not expect any change in interest rates at present.
"Current interest rates are appropriate and no need for adjustments," he said, responding to questions on whether the government would cut rates following rumours of a reduction.
The interest rate on one-year deposits was 7.47 percent, already lower than the interbank borrowing rate of around 11 percent, he said, but gave no further details.
